blocks.text: Simple lipids are esters of fatty acids with alcohols. They are subdivided by the type of alcohol into fats, oils and waxes.

Animal fats and vegetable oils are esters formed from one glycerol molecule and three fatty acids: triglycerides. The fatty acids may be the same or different. This structure makes them efficient energy-storage molecules and also provides insulation, protection of organs and a source of fat-soluble vitamins. Saturated fatty acids make lipids that are solid at room temperature (fats); oils contain unsaturated fatty acids with one or more double bonds. The hydrophobic fatty acid chains make fats insoluble in water but soluble in organic solvents; in the body this lets them form insulating layers under the skin and cushioning round organs such as the kidneys, helping with temperature regulation and protection.

Most waxes are long fatty acid chains esterified to long-chain alcohols. Both chains are non-polar and hydrophobic, so waxes form protective coatings that stop water sticking to surfaces. Natural waxes include beeswax, the oil in a whale's head, the coatings on the feathers of some water birds and plant waxes. They are used in pharmaceutical, cosmetic and other industries for lotions, ointments and polishes. A main component of beeswax is an ester such as myricyl palmitate, CH3(CH2)14-CO-O-(CH2)29CH3.

blocks.alt: Top: a triglyceride, a glycerol backbone CH2-CH-CH2 with three -O-CO- ester links to three zigzag fatty acid chains; notes say saturated chains give solid fats and unsaturated chains liquid oils, and list energy store, insulation and protection. Bottom left: a phospholipid, a round polar head with two zigzag tails. Bottom right: two rows of phospholipids with heads outward and tails inside, forming a bilayer.
blocks.caption: A triglyceride, a phospholipid and a lipid bilayer (original diagram after Figures 27.10 and 27.11).
blocks.long_description: Each OH group of glycerol forms an ester with one fatty acid, giving a triglyceride with three long non-polar tails. A phospholipid has only two fatty acids; its third position carries a polar phosphate group. In water, phospholipids line up with their water-loving heads facing the water and their tails tucked inside, forming the double layer of cell membranes.

blocks.title: The beeswax formula
blocks.text: The book prints the beeswax ester with chain lengths that do not match its usual main component; the lesson gives myricyl palmitate, CH3(CH2)14COO(CH2)29CH3. Flagged for review.

blocks.prompt: Why is olive oil a liquid while butter is a solid at room temperature?
blocks.explanation: Olive oil's triglycerides contain mainly unsaturated fatty acids, whose C=C bonds kink the chains so they pack poorly; butter contains more saturated fatty acids with straight chains that pack closely.

items: Simple lipids: esters of fatty acids with alcohols.
Triglycerides: glycerol + 3 fatty acids; fats (saturated, solid), oils (unsaturated, liquid).
Waxes: long-chain acid + long-chain alcohol; water-repellent coatings.
